page: Microsoft Azure D96nls_v6 is an x86_64 virtual machine instance within the Dnlv6 family, hosted on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system provides 96 dedicated Intel processor vCPUs alongside 192.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 2.0 GB per core memory profile. The instance includes no discrete graphics processing units and comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

This server type is designated as network-optimized and low-memory relative to standard general-purpose offerings. It operates without local disk storage, necessitating remote Premium Storage for operating system root disks and application data volumes. The reduced memory footprint shifts hardware resources toward thread density and parallel processing execution.

From an infrastructure efficiency perspective, the 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio avoids the overhead of unutilized RAM for tasks primarily bound by processor throughput. Eliminating onboard disk hardware also streamlines host resources for scenarios that rely strictly on remote networked storage architectures.

The D96nls_v6 is structured for workloads such as network-intensive microservices, CPU-bound batch processing, compilation clusters, and distributed compute jobs where working datasets do not require large per-core memory capacities.
description: Microsoft Azure D96nls_v6 is a network-optimized, low-memory virtual machine from the Dnlv6 series based on the x86_64 architecture. Managed by Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance features 96 dedicated Intel vCPUs and 192.0 GB of system memory, resulting in an allocation of 2.0 GB per core. The server contains no onboard local storage, relying on attached Premium Storage for operational file systems and persistent data. With zero GPUs and a 1:2 memory-to-core ratio, the instance is engineered to prioritize computational density over memory depth. This architecture fits horizontally scalable application layers, network-bound processing tasks, computational batch jobs, and distributed services requiring high core counts without extensive per-thread memory overhead.
